kept.mark: Entertainment Software Rating Board (ESRB) created
kept.mark_date_source: Entertainment Software Rating Board (intro: established in 1994)
kept.sentence: Mortal Kombat became one of the key games leading to the 1993 US Senate hearings on videogame violence, which led to the creation of the ESRB.
kept.notes: Well known pair. Night Trap shares the credit via the 1993 Senate hearings.

kept.mark: Australia's Commonwealth Classification Act and the Australian Classification Board
kept.mark_date_source: source sentence (came into force March 1, 1995); Australian Classification Board intro gives no date
kept.sentence: The Australian Senate had set up an inquiry in response to the original Mortal Kombat, Time Killers, and Night Trap, and the surrounding media coverage; the Senate's inquiry led to the Commonwealth Classification Act, which came into force on March 1, 1995, and introduced the Australian Classification Board.
kept.notes: Senate inquiry named Mortal Kombat, Time Killers and Night Trap. Less known outside Australia than the ESRB pair.

kept.mark: Japanese broadcasters' guidelines limiting flashing images in animation
kept.mark_date_source: Dennō Senshi Porygon, section Changes to television standards (guidelines established after the incident; no date given)
kept.sentence: Though the rules were never legally mandated, they were widely adopted across the Japanese animation industry as a result of the episode.
kept.notes: Guidelines set flicker limits (three per second with red, five without). The Porygon article says the UK Independent Television Commission took part. Exact adoption date needs a second source.

kept.stone: Super Bowl XXXVIII halftime show (Janet Jackson and Justin Timberlake)
kept.stone_article: Super Bowl XXXVIII halftime show controversy
kept.mark: YouTube founded
kept.mark_date_source: YouTube (intro: founded on February 14, 2005)
kept.sentence: YouTube co-founder Jawed Karim credits the incident with leading to the creation of the video sharing website.
kept.source_article: Super Bowl XXXVIII halftime show controversy
kept.notes: The founder's own account. The Legacy section also names the 2004 tsunami as a second trigger, so the halftime show is one of two named reasons. (Found by reading the section around a lexicon match; this sentence itself did not match the fixed lexicon.)

kept.stone: Super Bowl XXXVIII halftime show (Janet Jackson and Justin Timberlake)
kept.stone_article: Super Bowl XXXVIII halftime show controversy
kept.mark: Broadcast Decency Enforcement Act of 2005 (FCC fines raised to $325,000 per violation)
kept.mark_date_source: source sentence (by June 2006); mark article intro confirms passage by the 109th Congress
kept.sentence: By June 2006, the two houses reconciled the differences in fine levels, settling for a fine of US$325,000 per violation in the Broadcast Decency Enforcement Act of 2005.
kept.source_article: Super Bowl XXXVIII halftime show controversy
kept.notes: Section frames the Act as part of the crackdown that followed the broadcast. The 2004 version of the bill was proposed after the incident and did not pass. (Found by reading the section around a lexicon match; this sentence itself did not match the fixed lexicon.)

kept.stone: Super Bowl XXXVIII halftime show (Janet Jackson and Justin Timberlake)
kept.stone_article: Super Bowl XXXVIII halftime show controversy
kept.mark: Network rules requiring broadcast delays of up to five minutes on live events
kept.mark_date_source: source section (post-incident; no exact date)
kept.sentence: As a result of the incident, some networks established regulations requiring time delays of as much as five minutes for live broadcasts such as awards shows and sporting events.
kept.source_article: Super Bowl XXXVIII halftime show controversy
kept.notes: Policy is by unnamed networks; weaker than the two items above.

kept.mark: NASA's first orbiter named Enterprise
kept.mark_kind: institutional naming (outside the strict lasting-mark list)
kept.mark_date_source: Space Shuttle Enterprise (intro: rolled out September 17, 1976)
kept.sentence: The association between Star Trek and NASA grew stronger over time – the first NASA orbiter shuttle, Space Shuttle Enterprise, was named after the USS Enterprise of Star Trek fame.
kept.notes: Well known. Naming followed a fan write-in campaign. Kept as an institutional reaction; drop if namings are out of scope.

kept.mark: NASA names the ISS treadmill C.O.L.B.E.R.T.
kept.mark_kind: institutional naming (outside the strict lasting-mark list)
kept.mark_date_source: source sentence (NASA announcement April 15, 2009); mark article title redirects to the TVIS treadmill page
kept.mark_article: Combined Operational Load Bearing External Resistance Treadmill
kept.sentence: On April 15, 2009, NASA announced that instead of the new module being named after him, a treadmill on board the space station would be called the Combined Operational Load Bearing External Resistance Treadmill (C.O.L.B.E.R.T.).
kept.source_article: Cultural impact of The Colbert Report
kept.source_section: Places and things named for Colbert
kept.notes: NASA's response to Colbert winning an online vote to name Node 3. Surprising; naming, not a rule.

kept.mark: Charles and Drake v. State (Maryland appellate ruling on a CSI-effect voir dire question)
kept.mark_date_source: source paragraph (case dated 2010); no mark article
kept.sentence: In this case, the Maryland appellate court ruled the CSI effect voir dire question inappropriate due to its biased language and use of the term "convict" without mention of acquittal.
kept.notes: A court ruling exists because judges were asking jurors about a TV show. The juror effect itself is contested by studies cited in the same article; the ruling is not. Atkins v. State (2011) is a second ruling on a CSI-motivated jury instruction.

kept.mark: Canada makes the long-form census voluntary (National Household Survey)
kept.mark_date_source: 2011 Canadian census (intro: inaugural voluntary National Household Survey replaced the mandatory long form)
kept.sentence: This fact was referenced by the prime minister's office as a rationale for making the 40-page-long census form voluntary.
kept.notes: Chain: Star Wars, then 2001 Jedi write-ins (21,000 Canadians), then the PMO cites them as a rationale. One of several stated reasons; the 2010 decision itself is not dated in the source.

kept.mark: England and Wales census assigns Jedi Knight its own processing code (896)
kept.mark_date_source: 2001 United Kingdom census (census held 29 April 2001); code assignment year inferred from that census
kept.sentence: Jedi Knight was assigned its own code in England and Wales for census processing, numbered 896.
kept.notes: Measured by the official series: 390,127 in 2001, 176,632 in 2011, under 1,600 in 2021, so the behavior faded. Triggered by a 2001 chain email.

kept.mark: Comics Code Authority created
kept.mark_date_source: Comics Code Authority (intro: formed in 1954; Formation section: CMAA formed September 1954)
kept.sentence: Wertham's work resulted in the creation of the Comics Code, which drastically limited what kind of content could be published.
kept.notes: Well known. The 1954 Senate subcommittee hearings are a co-cause.

kept.mark: Comics Code revised to permit depicting narcotics addiction
kept.mark_date_source: Comics Code Authority, section Updating the Code (1971 revisions; narcotics change followed the May to July 1971 issues)
kept.sentence: As a result of publicity surrounding the Department of Health, Education and Welfare's sanctioning of the storyline, however, the CCA revised the Code to permit the depiction of "narcotics or drug addiction" if presented "as a vicious habit".
kept.notes: The issues ran without the Code seal at a federal health department's request; the Code changed as a result. Fairly well known among comics readers.

kept.stone_article: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
kept.mark: Real-life quidditch created as a team sport, later governed by the International Quidditch (now Quadball) Association
kept.mark_date_source: Quidditch (real-life sport) intro (created 2003); International Quadball Association intro (founded 2009)
kept.sentence: Quidditch, is a team sport that was created in 2003 at Nimbus 2003, a Harry Potter convention in Orlando, Florida, United States, and was inspired by the fictional game of the same name in the Harry Potter books by the author J.
kept.notes: Source article is the mark's own article. Governing body founded 2009.

kept.mark: "BTS Law": South Korea lets top pop artists defer mandatory military service to age 30
kept.mark_date_source: source paragraph (end of 2020); no mark article found
kept.sentence: At the end of the year, the "BTS Law" was passed by the National Assembly to allow its members to put off their mandated military service until they reach 30 years of age, instead of 28.
kept.notes: A conscription law amended for a band. Stone date is the 2013 debut (band formed 2010).

kept.mark: South Africa and Spain ban the Beatles from national radio
kept.mark_date_source: source section (pre-tour press conferences, August 1966)
kept.sentence: In Mexico City, there were demonstrations against the Beatles, and a number of countries banned the Beatles' music on national radio stations, including South Africa and Spain.
kept.notes: Duration not stated in the source; check a second source before calling it lasting.

kept.stone: Guy Fawkes mask (David Lloyd's design for V for Vendetta)
kept.mark: Saudi religious police prohibit wearing the mask
kept.mark_date_source: source sentence; Bahrain banned imports in February 2013 and Saudi Arabia banned imports in May 2013
kept.sentence: On 22 September 2013, Saudi religious police prohibited the wearing of the Guy Fawkes mask, the day before Saudi Arabia's 83rd National Day.
kept.notes: Bans react to the mask's protest use, which comes from the work. Chain runs through Anonymous and Arab Spring protesters. (Found by reading the section around a lexicon match; this sentence itself did not match the fixed lexicon.)

kept.mark: Thai military junta makes the three-finger salute illegal
kept.mark_date_source: source paragraph (aftermath of the 2014 Thai coup d'état; coup on 22 May 2014)
kept.sentence: Due to its use, the military announced that it would arrest anyone who displayed the salute and that the symbol was made illegal in Thailand.
kept.notes: Gesture popularized by the films; ban reacts to protest use. (Found by reading the section around a lexicon match; this sentence itself did not match the fixed lexicon.)

kept.mark: Waupun prison bans D&D as gang-related; the Seventh Circuit upholds the ban
kept.mark_date_source: source section Prisons (ban 2004; upheld January 25, 2010)
kept.sentence: In 2004, Wisconsin's Waupun Prison instituted a ban on playing Dungeons & Dragons, arguing that it promoted gang-related activity.
kept.notes: Idaho State Correctional Institution also bans role-playing games. Court ruling: Singer v. Raemisch (7th Cir. 2010). (Found by reading the section around a lexicon match; this sentence itself did not match the fixed lexicon.)

kept.mark: China bans South Park entirely
kept.mark_date_source: Band in China (intro: aired October 2, 2019; ban followed the release)
kept.sentence: The Chinese government banned South Park entirely following this episode's release, a move which in turn drew criticism from the creators of the show.
kept.notes: State ban of the work itself, but the episode was about Chinese censorship.

kept.mark: Children with access were 14 percent more likely to be at the right grade for their age (Kearney and Levine)
kept.mark_kind: durable behavior change measured by a study
kept.mark_date_source: Sesame Street research, section Later studies (study published 2019; outcomes from 1980 survey data)
kept.sentence: They also found that children who were able to watch the show were fourteen percent more likely to attend the grade that was appropriate for their age during their middle and high school years.
kept.notes: Natural experiment using 1969 broadcast coverage. Adjacent sentence to the lexicon match; the article also reports higher adult employment and wages. (Found by reading the section around a lexicon match; this sentence itself did not match the fixed lexicon.)

kept.stone: The Driller Killer (UK video release and advertising)
kept.mark: Video Recordings Act 1984 (BBFC certification required for videos)
kept.mark_date_source: Video Recordings Act 1984 (intro: passed in 1984; in force 1 September 1985 per Video nasty)
kept.sentence: This highly emotive coverage stirred up a frenzy among the general public which led to the Video Recordings Act being passed in 1984.
kept.notes: The film was released in 1979; its 1982 UK video adverts started the video nasty panic. Cannibal Holocaust and other titles share the credit. Well known in the UK.

kept.mark: UK refuses the film Mikey
kept.mark_date_source: Video nasty, section Relaxation of censorship
kept.sentence: Claims, since proven at best to be speculative, at worst outright media fabrication, relating to the Hungerford massacre and the murder of James Bulger (where the 1991 film Child's Play 3 was erroneously held up as influencing the perpetrators, possibly prompting the 1992 film Mikey to be prohibited in the UK), provided an additional impetus to restrict films and as late as December 1997, the board claimed it "has never relaxed its guidelines on video violence, which remain the strictest in the world".
kept.notes: Disputed: the article calls the Bulger link erroneous and the effect on Mikey 'possibly'.

kept.mark: Hollywood begins enforcing the Production Code
kept.mark_date_source: Motion Picture Production Code (intro: applied 1934 to 1968)
kept.sentence: Though in place, the Hays Code was not enforced until 1934, spurred on in response to objections voiced by several groups to the content of Hollywood films – provoked at least partly by the notorious 1933 Czech film Ecstasy, which was highly controversial in its time largely because of a nude swimming scene by Hedy Lamarr as well as perhaps the first non-pornographic film to portray sexual intercourse, although never showing more than the actors' faces.
kept.notes: 'At least partly': one of several provocations. Surprising: a Czech art film helped trigger Code enforcement.

kept.mark: Film banned in all United States military establishments
kept.mark_date_source: Paths of Glory, section Controversy
kept.sentence: The film was banned in all United States military establishments, both at home and overseas, due to its content.
kept.notes: Same section: Swiss government banned showings until 1970; France saw it only in 1975.

kept.mark: Swiss government bans all presentations of the film until 1970
kept.mark_date_source: Paths of Glory, section Controversy
kept.sentence: The Swiss government banned any presentations of the film until 1970 on the grounds that it was "incontestably offensive" to France, its judicial system, and its army.
kept.notes: A neutral country banning a US film for offending France's army.

kept.mark: Polish municipal council names a village street after Obi-Wan Kenobi
kept.mark_kind: institutional naming (outside the strict lasting-mark list)
kept.mark_date_source: Obi-Wan Kenobi Street, section History (accepted 30 December 2004)
kept.sentence: The street is named after Obi-Wan Kenobi, a fictional character in the Star Wars franchise.
kept.notes: Gmina Lubicz council, village of Grabowiec. Naming, not a rule.

kept.mark: BBC bans its own commissioned film from broadcast for 20 years
kept.mark_date_source: BBC controversies, section 1965: The War Game (banned 1965; first screened 1985)
kept.sentence: Intended for the twentieth anniversary on 6 August 1965 of the dropping of the bomb on Hiroshima, The War Game was banned by the BBC, which said it was "too horrifying for the medium of broadcasting".
kept.notes: The film won an Oscar for best documentary while banned from the channel that made it.

kept.mark: Texas "Save Our Swifties" law banning bots that bulk-buy tickets
kept.mark_date_source: Political impact of Taylor Swift, section Legislative action (signed May 22, 2023); no mark article
kept.sentence: On May 22, 2023, Texas governor Greg Abbott signed the "Save Our Swifties" bill into law, banning the use of bots to bulk-purchase tickets.
kept.notes: Section header says Swift inspired these bills; the November 2022 Eras Tour presale failure is the implied trigger but is not stated in this section. Minnesota's "Taylor Swift bill" (fee disclosure) was signed in May 2024.
